findings.title: fractional() loses or corrupts the sign for negative fractions
findings.cause: The function splits the number with int(number), which truncates negative values toward zero, then takes abs(numerator) for values with no whole-number part and leaves a negative numerator for mixed fractions.
findings.impact: Negative inputs can be rendered as positive fractions, or as malformed mixed fractions such as '-1 -3/10'. This is a data-preservation bug because the sign and therefore the numeric meaning are changed or made ambiguous.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:370 computes whole_number = int(number)
src/humanize/number.py:379 returns abs(numerator) when whole_number is zero
src/humanize/number.py:382 formats the signed numerator directly for mixed fractions
focused probe: fractional(-0.3) -> '3/10'; fractional(-1.3) -> '-1 -3/10'; fractional('-8.9') -> '-8 -9/10'
findings.reproduction_or_test:
uv run python - <<'PY'
import humanize
assert humanize.fractional(-0.3) == '-3/10'
assert humanize.fractional(-1.3) == '-1 3/10'
PY

findings.title: intcomma() does not group negative numbers
findings.cause: After converting the value to text, grouping is applied with the regex ^(\d+)(\d{3}), which only matches strings beginning with digits. A leading '-' prevents every grouping pass.
findings.impact: Negative integers and floats are returned without thousands separators, including localized decimal strings after normalization. That breaks the function's core promise for a common numeric boundary.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:167 builds orig = str(value)
src/humanize/number.py:172 uses a digit-only start anchor
tests/test_number.py:41-83 covers positive values and infinities but no finite negative intcomma inputs
findings.reproduction_or_test:
uv run python - <<'PY'
import humanize
assert humanize.intcomma(-1000) == '-1,000'
assert humanize.intcomma(-1234567.89) == '-1,234,567.89'
PY

findings.title: ordinal() uses the wrong suffix for negative integers
findings.cause: Suffix selection uses value % 100 and value % 10 directly on signed integers. Python modulo for negatives does not produce the absolute last digits needed for ordinal suffix rules.
findings.impact: Negative ordinals are rendered incorrectly, for example '-1th', '-2th', '-3th', and '-21th'. The docstring says the function works for any integer, but tests only cover positive integers.
evidence: src/humanize/number.py:76 coerces input to int
src/humanize/number.py:105 checks value % 100
src/humanize/number.py:107 indexes suffixes with value % 10
tests/test_number.py:14-38 has no negative ordinal cases
focused probe: ordinal(-1) -> '-1th'; ordinal(-2) -> '-2th'; ordinal(-3) -> '-3th'; ordinal(-8) -> '-8nd'; ordinal(-21) -> '-21th'
findings.reproduction_or_test:
uv run python - <<'PY'
import humanize
assert humanize.ordinal(-1) == '-1st'
assert humanize.ordinal(-2) == '-2nd'
assert humanize.ordinal(-3) == '-3rd'
assert humanize.ordinal(-21) == '-21st'
PY

findings.title: naturalsize() crashes on NaN and assigns byte units to infinities
findings.cause: The function converts input with float(value) but never checks math.isfinite before taking logarithms, converting the exponent to int, and selecting a suffix.
findings.impact: NaN raises ValueError, while +inf and -inf are rendered as 'inf QB' and '-inf QB'. Other public numeric functions in this package return explicit non-finite sentinels such as 'NaN', '+Inf', and '-Inf', so this API is inconsistent and misleading for non-finite floats or strings.
evidence: src/humanize/filesize.py:90 converts value to float
src/humanize/filesize.py:99 computes int(min(log(abs_bytes, base), len(suffix))) without a finite check
tests/test_filesize.py:9-97 covers finite positive and negative values but no NaN or infinity cases
focused probe: naturalsize(math.nan) -> ValueError; naturalsize(math.inf) -> 'inf QB'; naturalsize(-math.inf) -> '-inf QB'
findings.reproduction_or_test:
uv run python - <<'PY'
import humanize, math
assert humanize.naturalsize(math.nan) == 'NaN'
assert humanize.naturalsize(math.inf) == '+Inf'
assert humanize.naturalsize(-math.inf) == '-Inf'
PY

findings.title: time delta APIs leak OverflowError for infinite float inputs
findings.cause: naturaldelta catches only ValueError and TypeError around int(value) and timedelta conversion, while int(math.inf) raises OverflowError. naturaltime and precisedelta route through _date_and_delta, which also catches only ValueError and TypeError around round(value) or timedelta construction.
findings.impact: Passing math.inf or -math.inf crashes naturaldelta(), naturaltime(), and precisedelta() instead of returning the input unchanged or a stable sentinel. This contradicts the naturaldelta return contract that non-convertible inf/nan values are returned unchanged, and it leaves public formatting APIs with inconsistent non-finite behavior.
evidence: src/humanize/time.py:112-116 documents returning the value unchanged when it cannot be converted because of 'inf' or 'nan'
src/humanize/time.py:148-153 catches only ValueError and TypeError in naturaldelta
src/humanize/time.py:86-91 catches only ValueError and TypeError in _date_and_delta
src/humanize/time.py:534-536 shows precisedelta relies on _date_and_delta for invalid input fallback
focused probe: naturaldelta(math.inf), naturaltime(math.inf), and precisedelta(math.inf) all raise OverflowError
